Retention activates class-deletion fences only after earlier serialized opt-in migration work settles, so retention cannot supersede or strand a migration record and exports remain blocked until migration and retention converge

Repair journals are HMAC-authenticated and bound to a profile authority, monotonic repair epoch, stable operation ID, token hash and original database identity; completed, tampered and cross-profile journals fail closed before database, key or anchor mutation

Every repair phase advances two HMAC-chained, append-only high-water copies outside the replaceable database, anchor and journal set; either current copy rejects restored older journal-authority pairs and populated replacement databases fail closed

Database repair durably enters an authenticated erasing-database phase before its first header write, then safely resumes absent or raw-header-corrupt originals without opening SQLite while wrong identities and unreadable databases outside that active phase are never erased

Fresh repair creation durably assigns and HMAC-binds an exact database identity and repair epoch before schema creation; only that pristine identity can resume, and every persisted table, metadata key, clock and non-default setting is checked before adoption

Each high-water marker is written through a fsynced temporary file and atomic durable rename; copies are parsed independently so one torn trailing copy is rebuilt from the intact authenticated chain while both-torn and divergent valid chains fail closed

Fresh-profile repair security bootstrap is a resumable epoch-zero transaction: partial key, dual high-water or authority writes are reconstructed only while no repair journal, receipt, completed database binding or post-zero high-water exists and the database remains pristine and unmodified

Completed repair journal cleanup atomically renames the authenticated live journal to a cleanup artifact before secure erase; crash recovery removes unreadable cleanup artifacts only when matching authority, dual high-water, receipt and current database binding prove the same completed repair

Opt-out and explicit D3 deletion supersede failed persistence-migration recovery before any stale roster, Passport or D3 evidence can be republished, while the destructive operation retains the authoritative recovery barrier through commit

D1 and D2 deletion during incomplete opt-in atomically rebases the durable migration marker to the new privacy generation, erases only the selected class from its Passport and canonical event payload, and preserves resumable sanitized work for every remaining class

Every ordinary Passport mutation uses its canonical event dedupe key as a stable authenticated operation receipt; ambiguous commits retain an export and mutation barrier until bounded authoritative event and Passport reconciliation proves committed durable state or explicit non-success

Persistence clients dispatch only initialize until initialization succeeds; every initialization failure consumes the bounded restart budget, settles queued callers, opens the circuit on exhaustion and cannot surface an unhandled service readiness rejection

Passport repair artifact publication uses MoveFileExW with MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING and MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH on Windows, propagates native failures without an unrelated SQLite flush fallback, and durably renames securely erased files out of authoritative paths before best-effort removal

The controlled privacy form tracks authoritative baselines and dirty fields independently, rebases destructive opt-out immediately, preserves non-conflicting retention edits and blocks overlapping stale edits from silently re-enabling D3 persistence

An authoritative D1 or D2 deletion receipt atomically replaces the exact pending deletion recovery with its rebased sanitized migration recovery without exposing an unblocked interval, so export, retry and restart converge instead of deadlocking on operation identity

A recovered canonical close receipt idempotently moves the exact durable closed Passport into bounded history once, clears current challenge and readiness state, survives restart without duplication and permits subsequent telemetry to start a new stint
